meta.title: Agent Prompt Research · Pilot report
meta.description: Evidence-backed report from a completed Agent Prompt Research pilot.

hero.eyebrow: Completed engineering pilot · 9 valid cells · 3 tasks × 3 variants
hero.title: Use the leanest prompt that is still sufficient.
hero.lede: All A/B/C variants achieved 3/3 task success and zero unrelated edits. Lean A was most efficient on aggregate input tokens and latency; Structured B produced the smallest average diff.
hero.scope: This is descriptive n=3-tasks-per-variant evidence—not a universal claim that short prompts are better.

results.title: Key results
results.note: Codex input tokens include large cached/base agent context. Prompt-character differences are only one contributor; prompt chars must not be equated directly with total input tokens.

comparison.title: Experiment comparison
comparison.caption: Aggregate comparison of prompt variants
comparison.note: A used 23.77% fewer mean input tokens than B and 32.37% fewer than C. B's mean diff was 35% below A and 52.29% below C. Retry is an operational test-invocation proxy, not provider retry telemetry.

tasks.title: Task-level results
tasks.caption: Per-task results
tasks.note: Per-task results are non-monotonic: t2/C's prompt was longer than t2/B's but used fewer input tokens and lower latency. Runtime context, caching, task details, and model behavior may contribute.

evidence.eyebrow: What kind of evidence is this?
evidence.title: External evidence tiers
evidence.officialText: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft guidance favors clear goals, critical constraints, and procedure when sequence genuinely matters.
evidence.peerText: AgentIF and context studies support concern about complexity or context use. APEX is counter-evidence to any universal shorter-is-better rule.
evidence.preprintText: The Prompt Report is used for taxonomy and landscape only.
evidence.pilotText: One model/runtime, three small deterministic JavaScript tasks, one run per cell. Results are useful for decisions in this setting, not generalization.

framework.title: Prompt decision framework
framework.step1: Include relevant domain context, allowed side effects, correctness contract, success test, evidence, and approval boundary.
framework.step2: Delete repetition, stale examples, irrelevant tools, and process narration—while retaining details whose omission could change correctness, safety, semantics, approvals, or evidence.
framework.step3: Use ordered steps when sequence/completeness is itself required or representative evals show a reliability gap.
framework.step4: Track success first, then scope/diff, latency, tokens, and retry proxies. Recheck after model, tool, runtime, or domain changes.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.text: No statistical power, significance testing, or causal identification. The pilot uses one model/runtime, one run per task/variant, three small deterministic JavaScript tasks, and limited agent-domain diversity. Caching, order, environment effects, and runtime variability may affect resource measures. Provider usage and the retry field have the definitions documented in the report.

repro.title: Reproducibility and links
repro.text: Official agent runs are complete and raw inputs are frozen. Verify the aggregate and integrity manifest locally; do not rerun the official matrix as ordinary QA.

footer.description: Agent Prompt Research · completed pilot · descriptive evidence

tracks.title: Research tracks
tracks.intro: Instruction density and agent collaboration are related, but they are not the same experiment. Each track keeps its own protocol, evidence, and claims.
tracks.promptText: Tests when lean outcome-first prompts preserve success while reducing unnecessary instruction overhead.
tracks.tcmText: Tests whether teammate behaviors—shared goal, context continuity, calibrated initiative, constructive disagreement, and trust calibration—reduce collaboration friction beyond friendly tone alone.

tcm.metaTitle: Trusted Colleague Model · Agent Prompt Research
tcm.metaDescription: Trusted Colleague Model research protocol for low-friction human-AI collaboration.
tcm.title: Trusted Colleague Model
tcm.lede: Can an AI agent work more naturally and effectively by behaving like a competent, context-aware colleague—not by pretending to be human, but by sharing the goal, exercising judgment, and reducing collaboration friction?
tcm.noResults: Protocol only. No TCM experiment has been run yet, so this page reports hypotheses and design—not findings.
tcm.principle: A good AI colleague should be competent, predictable, context-aware, appropriately proactive, willing to challenge material mistakes, and clear about uncertainty.
tcm.dimGoalText: Optimize for the real outcome and notice obvious gaps, without taking authority away from the user.
tcm.dimContextText: Carry forward valid decisions, constraints, blockers, and evidence instead of restarting each turn.
tcm.dimMonitorText: Catch material assumptions or errors and provide task-relevant backup when a gap would block success.
tcm.dimChallengeText: Say when a proposal is risky or weak, explain why, and avoid both automatic agreement and needless contrarianism.
tcm.dimAdaptText: Know when to continue, when to ask, and how strongly to review or execute based on task risk and uncertainty.
tcm.dimTrustText: Separate verified facts from inference and communicate directly without rigid report templates or fake familiarity.
tcm.conditionsIntro: Model, reasoning, tools, safety, context, and task stay the same. The communication/collaboration contract changes.
tcm.condAText: Competent professional baseline: clear and structured, without an explicit teammate-behavior contract.
tcm.condBText: Same baseline behavior with warmer, less bureaucratic wording. This isolates friendly tone.
tcm.condCText: Fixed peer stance with shared-goal behavior, monitoring, backup, constructive disagreement, and calibrated certainty.
tcm.condDText: TCM plus a temporary Peer, Senior, Specialist, Reviewer, or Operator stance chosen for the current task—not a fixed role router.
tcm.blindText: Generation order and evaluation order are independently randomized. Evaluators see neutral response IDs, not condition labels or the expected winner.
tcm.outcomeSuccess: Task Success — did the response satisfy prewritten acceptance criteria?
tcm.outcomeFit: Colleague Fit — does it behave like a competent, reliable work partner?
tcm.outcomeFriction: Collaboration Friction Score — how much avoidable correction, repetition, confirmation, or extra-turn effort did the user need?
tcm.outcomeContinue: Willingness to Continue — would the evaluator keep working with this agent?
tcm.analysisText: Planned analysis controls for task and rater effects, reports effect sizes and uncertainty, tests response length as a sensitivity variable, and keeps safety/factual accuracy as non-negotiable guardrails.
tcm.evidenceEyebrow: Theory informs the test; it does not pre-decide the result
tcm.sourceBigFiveText: Provides teamwork constructs such as mutual monitoring, backup behavior, adaptability, shared mental models, closed-loop communication, and trust.
tcm.sourceSmmTitle: Shared mental models in human-AI teams
tcm.sourceSmmText: Motivates testing whether aligned task/role understanding helps humans and AI predict needs and coordinate more effectively.
tcm.sourceTeammateText: A large online experiment found teammate presentation changed trust and interaction sentiment, supporting relationship framing as a variable worth testing.
tcm.sourceMisunderstandingText: Human-AI teamwork evidence links information omission and communication breakdowns with trust and performance effects.
tcm.evidenceBoundary: These sources motivate constructs and hypotheses. None directly proves that TCM will improve software-engineering or ERP-agent work; that is what the planned experiment must test.
tcm.boundaryTitle: Colleague behavior without pretending to be human
tcm.boundaryText: TCM does not ask an AI to claim feelings, identity, authority, or human responsibility. Over-initiative, fake familiarity, excessive disagreement, stale-context overreach, unsupported certainty, and length inflation are explicit failure modes.
tcm.footer: Trusted Colleague Model · PRE-PILOT · no experimental findings yet
